TRANSITIONS is computed eagerly at module import time via load_transitions(), so any missing, extra, duplicate or semantically altered transition (a wrong source, event/guard, durable effect or destination) raises FSMTableIntegrityError before the module can even finish importing, failing both local startup and CI collection -- the task's own negative acceptance criterion made structural rather than merely tested for.

design: GovernedActionFSM.apply() looks up any of the 44 transitions by id and always durably persists an immutable PersistedEffect record (transition_id, source, destination, durable_effect text, a timezone-aware timestamp via the shared require_aware, correlation_id, and an immutable context mapping) through an injected sink before returning -- proving every declared effect is persisted, complementing (not duplicating) OCOR-DEV-0030's own executable slice of the single representative path's four real gates. An unknown transition id is refused (FSMTransitionError, reason_code=UNKNOWN_TRANSITION) before the sink is ever called; a sink failure propagates rather than being silently swallowed, and a retry against the same FSM instance succeeds cleanly.

residual_risks: This task builds the complete 44-transition table plus a generic effect-persistence mechanism, but does not itself implement the substantive domain semantics of every one of the 44 declared effects (e.g. 'registra proposta, GCS, fingerprint ed Evidence') -- that remains each real component's own responsibility, as OCOR-DEV-0030's engine.py already demonstrates for the four gates on the single representative path. A future task wiring a specific transition's real domain effect would call GovernedActionFSM.apply() alongside its own real logic, not instead of it.

GovernedActionFSM's per-instance table is immutable and does not itself detect a future, still-unsealed edit to docs/OCOR_LLD_v1.1.md at runtime after import (only at the moment TRANSITIONS is computed); this mirrors OCOR-DEV-0020's own sealed spike's design and is an accepted, already-established limitation of a load-once table, not a new gap.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.
